newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia sugarbeet area well under target - expert.
newsitem.headline: Serbia sugarbeet area well under target - expert.

text.p: Serbia expects to sow 50,000-60,000 hectares with sugarbeet this year, well below the government's target of 100,000 ha under the crop, industry sources said Wednesday.

"We expect between 50,000 and 60,000 hectares to be sown under sugarbeet but will only know the final area in mid-May when we see what damage weeds, disease and pests have wrought," Jugosecer sugar producers association expert Milan Patkovic told Reuters.
The government's planned acreage is based on the total capacity of Yugoslavia's sugar refineries at around 4.5 million tonnes of sugarbeet.
So far, sowing has been completed on around 48,000 ha.
Official statistics estimate the 1996 sugarbeet area at 70,000 ha.
Patkovic said the association expected at least two million tonnes of beet would be produced in 1997, a drop on last year's crop around 2.5 million tonnes.
One of the reasons for the sowings shortfall is the government's failure to pay its debt to farmers for their 1996 crops.
"So far only half of the debt has been repaid," he said.
An industry analyst cautioned that late government payments would have a negative effect on this year's production.
So far, Yugoslav sugar refineries have concluded deals for beet sowing on 57,400 hectares and more are expected to be reached before the sowing campaign ends, said Patkovic.
Another reason is excessive sugar imports last year which hurt domestic sugar production, he said. Last year, 180,000 tonnes of sugar were imported and sold at lower prices than domestic sugar.
"There is enough sugar stock now until the harvest and it will be good for domestic producers if no more sugar is imported," Patkovic said.
The beet sowing campaign is due to end between April 15 and 20, depending on weather.
"The light rainfall forecast for the next few days can only be favourable for the beet," Patkovic said. --Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 4305
